title: RTP750FP (NSIC Rc 824H) Hybrid Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: RTP750FP (NSIC Rc 824H): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: RTP750FP is NSIC Rc 824H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland: about 108 days and 8.3 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 824H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as RTP750FP and known locally as Mestiso 176. The NSIC approved it in 2026. RiceTec bred it. It matures in about 108 days and averages 8.3 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 8.7 tonnes in trials.

heroImage.alt: Ripe palay heads, the harvest a hybrid like NSIC Rc 824H is bred to fill

blocks.text: If you came here looking for RTP750FP, or rice variety 824H, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 8.3 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 166 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 8.7 tonnes.
**Holds up against:** green leafhopper, stem borer, rice blast.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.caption: From PhilRice's catalogue of released varieties (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 824H yield?

On average it gives 8.3 tonnes per hectare. That is about 166 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 180 irrigated lowland hybrids in PhilRice's list, which is 6.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 8.7 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 108 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is RTP750FP the same as NSIC Rc 824H?
items.a: Yes. RTP750FP is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 824H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 176. The numbers on this page are PhilRice's for NSIC Rc 824H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 824H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 176. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 824H take to harvest?
items.a: About 108 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 824H?
items.a: PhilRice lists 8.3 tonnes per hectare on average, about 166 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 8.7 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
